claims.text: A hybrid free-energy integration framework can combine sparse on-the-fly ab initio molecular-dynamics sampling with a machine-learning surrogate.
The proposed framework can retain electron–vibration coupling and anharmonic effects through corrections.
The framework can achieve approximately 90% fidelity relative to full explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The framework can reduce computational cost by a factor of 10–100.
Targeted ab initio molecular-dynamics samples can represent key configurational regions in both solid and liquid phases.
An ML surrogate trained on targeted ab initio samples can interpolate the relevant free-energy landscape.
Perturbative reweighting can accurately capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
Continuous refinement of the surrogate using sparse ab initio data and perturbative corrections will provide an adequate structural mediator for free-energy prediction.
Selective use of expensive ab initio sampling will preserve essential thermodynamic contributions while lowering computational demand.
Predicted phase free-energy differences will remain within approximately 10% of full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
Predicted latent heats will remain within approximately 10% of full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
Predicted specific-heat curves will remain within approximately 10% of full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
For multicomponent systems, the method will be 10–100 times more computationally efficient than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluation and TOR-TILD have high fidelity.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluation and TOR-TILD are computationally expensive, especially for complex multicomponent systems.
The method is expected to be robust near fusion conditions for elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Extreme electron–vibration coupling or highly complex multicomponent systems may reduce surrogate fidelity.
